subject: general
question:
In a certain code language,

‘A + B’ means ‘A is the daughter of B’,

‘A - B’ means ‘A is the husband of B’,

‘A × B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’ and

‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the father of B’.

How is B related to D, if A × B + C ÷ D?

A × B → A is the mother of B.

B + C → B is the daughter of C.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cf0e6a33410433e81999b8a5942a38fc1bd1ab774cd92a01cf56be5e1455d356.png] 

C ÷ D → C is the father of D.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/abb54c3d219ea539e9bb0843fd4118ba0167eabb1f23013f9f00aa7271206807.png] 

Thus, B is the sister of D.

Hence, "Option 2" is the correct answer.
